column9: Series consists of records created in the different stages of forest resource inventory.  Series includes aerial photography and related key maps, indices and flight reports.  Series also includes forest resource inventory data and maps, showing the area, volume and type of forest resources in surveyed and unsurveyed areas of the province as well as reports and correspondence documenting how the forest resource inventory was conducted.  Series is arranged into sixteen sub-series based on record type or subject.

column35: Efforts at inventorying Ontario's forests began in the 1920s, but by the end of World War II the information accumulated offered only a general picture of conditions and was not detailed enough to enable the creation of forest management plans for specific areas.  In 1946 the production of a detailed forest resources inventory commenced when the Photographic Survey Company and Department of Lands and Forests staff began to produce aerial photographs and planimetric maps of an 140,000 square mile area of northern Ontario.  Armed with these photographs and maps, working teams of foresters laid out tenth-of-an-acre plots in the field, measuring trees and tallying species. Information on stand content was recorded on the aerial photographs;  subsequently, it was classified and typed onto 4 inch to a mile planimetric maps.In 1951 the federal government agreed to fund 50% of the cost, and the project area was doubled in size to include southern Ontario.   Originally, the plan was to reinventory areas every 10 years. Currently, reinventorying occurs every 20 years.  Inventorying is a three year process:  the first year, aerial photographs are taken;  the second year, plots are delineated by air photo interpreters, field work takes place, and stands are described; in the third year, maps are drafted.  In 1986 the mapping process was automated.
